title: Sparse conditional circuits: a router executes K of E modules per token
follows: R1.03 (queue order); independent of it: tested on the plain Transformer so that the mechanism has its own evidence
question: At equal active compute, does a top-2-of-8 module bank beat a dense MLP on the micro-benchmark, and does the router specialise by task beyond what token identity alone explains?

predictions.S1_vs_active_matched: moe-top2 ID accuracy >= transformer + 0.02, OOD >= transformer - 0.01, at <= 1.15x its FLOPs.
predictions.S2_vs_total_matched: moe-top2 ID accuracy >= transformer-wide - 0.02 at <= 0.5x its FLOPs.
predictions.S3_specialisation: Token-conditioned task-expert NMI, I(task; expert | token) / H(task | token), >= 0.1 and >= 2x the same router's value at initialisation, with every expert above 2% load. (The unconditional NMI is reported but not used: an untrained router already scores 0.11 on it because tasks use different tokens.)

decision.PARTIAL: (S1 or S2) without S3, or S3 alone.

not_claimed: Mixture-of-Experts is prior art. No novelty claim.
benchmark_note: Changed before any run (2026-09-29): microbench v1's hops task let 'the digit at the end of the longest chain' answer 91% ID / 100% OOD without following the query (found while auditing R1.02's benchmark). microbench2 uses two equal chains (50% guess); state and recall are unchanged. tests/test_r103.py audits cues. Models, budget and gate thresholds are unchanged.
